not_covered: Microsoft's Recall feature became a privacy scandal in 2024 because, despite claims that data was encrypted, security researchers demonstrated that screenshots were stored unencrypted (in plaintext) within a local SQLite database [Source: ev-1].
This allowed any process running as the user to access sensitive information captured by default, including passwords and private content visible on screen [Source: ev-1].

The incident drew scrutiny from regulatory bodies such as the Irish Data Protection Commission, the UK Information Commissioner's Office, and an investigation opened by Washington State Attorney General Bob Ferguson [Source: ev-1].
In response, Microsoft changed the feature significantly.[Source: ev-1]
This revised version reached general availability on Copilot+ PCs in 2025 [Source: ev-1].
